It is of two kinds: sending of religion, which He loves and is pleased with, such as His sending of His messengers and prophets; and sending of creation (kawn), which is also of two kinds. One kind He loves and is pleased with, such as His sending of His angels to manage the affairs of His creation. This is supported by the fact that angels are assigned to the winds to drive them and direct them. A group said: they are the angels who spread their wings in the air when they ascend and descend.

It was said: they spread out God's commands over the earth and the heavens.

It was said: they spread out souls, giving them life through faith.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿as an excuse or as a warning﴾ (77:6)

(Section)

Some people say: among the completions of repentance is abandoning making excuses (i'tidhar), for making excuses is an argument against the offense, while abandoning excuses is an acknowledgment of it, and repentance is not valid except after acknowledgment. Regarding this, one of the poets said to his superior, when he had blamed him for something:

"You did not meet your reproach with an excuse, but I say what you say.
And I knock at the door of your pardon with humility, and good character judges between us."

When the superior heard his words, he stood up, rode to him immediately, and removed his blame.

So the completion of acknowledgment is abandoning excuses, by having in his heart and tongue: "O God, I have no innocence from sin so that I might make an excuse, and I have no strength so that I might prevail. Rather, I am a sinner seeking forgiveness. O God, I have no excuse; it is purely Your right and purely my offense. If You pardon, well and good; otherwise the right is Yours."

What appears to me from the words of the author of Manazil al-Sa'irin is that by making excuses he meant showing weakness and humility, the enemy's dominance, and the strength of the authority of the soul. He meant that what came from me was not out of contempt for Your right, nor out of ignorance of it, nor out of denying Your knowledge, nor out of making light of Your threat. Rather, it came from the overpowering of desire and the weakness of strength to resist the sickness of lust, and out of hope for Your forgiveness, reliance on Your pardon, good opinion of You, hope in Your generosity, and desire for the vastness of Your forbearance and mercy. The delusion deceived me about You, along with the commanding soul to evil, and Your concealing veil over me. My ignorance aided me, and there is no way to seek protection for me except through You, and no help for obedience to You except through Your guidance. And similar to this are words containing supplication, humbling oneself, need, acknowledgment of incapacity, and affirmation of servitude.

This is among the completions of repentance. Only the wise, who seek to win favor with their Lord, mighty and majestic, adopt it, and God loves that His servant seek to win His favor.

In a hadith: "Seek to win God's favor." And in the Sahih (the authentic collection of hadith): "No one loves excuse more than God." Even if its meaning is that of giving excuse (i'dhar), as He said at the end of the hadith: "For this reason He sent the messengers as bearers of good tidings and warners."

And He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Then those that deliver the reminder, as an excuse or as a warning﴾ (77:5–6). It is part of His perfect justice and kindness that He gave excuse to His servants, and that He does not punish their wrongdoers except after the full giving of excuse and the establishment of proof against them. So He also loves that His servant make excuse before Him and seek release from his sin before Him.

In a hadith: "Whoever makes excuse to God, God accepts his excuse."

This is the praiseworthy and beneficial excuse.

As for making excuses by destiny (al-qadar), it is a contesting with God and an argument by the servant against the Lord, and placing the blame for his sin upon the decrees. This is the act of God's adversaries, as one of their shaykhs said regarding His saying: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾ (3:14). This ignorant man lied about God and His speech. What is meant by it is to discourage from this perishing, passing world, to encourage the enduring, lasting one, and to disparage those who prefer this adorned thing and follow it. It is like a child to whom are shown toys to play with, so he becomes excited by them and moves toward them, although the one who adorned them is not mentioned. So He did not say "We were adorned for people." God, Exalted is He, attributes the adorning of the world and of sins to the devils, as He said: ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear good to them﴾ (6:43), and He said: ﴿And thus their partners have made the killing of their children appear attractive to many of the polytheists﴾ (6:137).

In a hadith: "I was sent as a guide and a caller, and I have no share of guidance. Iblis was sent as a misleader and one who adorns, and he has no share of error." This does not contradict His saying: ﴿Thus We made attractive to every community its deeds﴾ (6:108).

And when he says: 'O Lord, I wronged myself, I erred, I transgressed, I did it,' God, mighty and majestic, says: 'I had power over you, I decreed it, I wrote it, and I forgive you.' And when he does a good deed and says: 'O Lord, I did it, I gave charity, I prayed, I fed,' God, mighty and majestic, says: 'I helped you, I granted you success.' And when he says: 'O Lord, You helped me and granted me success, and You bestowed favor upon me,' God says: 'You did it, You willed it, You earned it.'"

So making excuse is of two kinds: an excuse that negates acknowledgment, which contradicts repentance; and an excuse that affirms acknowledgment, which is part of the completion of repentance.

The Qur'an never uses this plural except in the masculine plural, not the feminine. Also, the word's conjunction with what follows, which is the oath, does not suit interpreting it as the prophets. Furthermore, in the Qur'an the messengers are those sworn upon, not those sworn by, as in His saying: ﴿By God, We certainly sent (messengers) to nations before you﴾ (16:63), and His saying: ﴿And indeed you are among the messengers﴾ (36:3), and His saying: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an, indeed you are among the messengers﴾ (36:1–3).

If the custom is taken as the custom of the follower, like the "'urf" of a horse (its mane, which falls in one direction), the "'urf" of a rooster (its comb), and the saying "the people are to so-and-so in one 'urf," meaning they are in one direction, racing toward him in their intention and their turning toward him, then it is permissible for al-mursalat to be the winds, and this is supported by the conjunction of al-'asifat (those that blow with violence) and al-nashirat (those that spread) after it. It is also permissible for them to be the angels. And it is permissible for it to include both types, since the sending is customarily applied to both. This is supported by the fact that angels are assigned to the winds to drive them and direct them. The winds are also supported as the meaning by the conjunction of al-'asifat to it with the fa' of sequence and causation, as if they were sent and then they blew violently. Whoever takes al-mursalat as the angels says that they blow violently in their rapid passing, just as the winds blow violently. But most scholars hold that they are the winds.

There is a third view: that they blow violently against the soul of the disbeliever. It is said: "'asafa bi-al-shay'" when one destroys and annihilates it. Al-A'sha said:

"It blows violently against the shield and the bare-headed one..."

Abu Ishaq related this.

But this is a forced view, because what is sworn by must necessarily be a sign, an apparent thing indicating lordship. As for unseen matters that are believed in, they are what is sworn upon. God, glory be to Him, swears by His angels and His book because their matter is manifest and because there are clear proofs and signs indicating their existence.

As for ﴿those that spread (clouds) widely﴾ (al-nashirat nashran), it is the beginning of another oath, and this is why it is introduced with the waw (and). What came before it is conjoined with the first oath with the fa'.

Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: they are the winds that bring rain. This is supported by His saying: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ (7:57).

That is, they spread out the clouds widely, which is the opposite of folding up.

Muqatil said: they are the angels that spread out the records of the children of Adam and their deeds. Masruq and Ata' from Ibn Abbas also said this.

A group said: they are the angels who spread their wings in the air when they ascend and descend.

It was said: they spread out God's commands over the earth and the heavens.

It was said: they spread out souls, giving them life through faith.

Abu Salih said: they are the rains that spread over the earth, meaning they give it life.

I say: It is permissible for al-nashirat to be intransitive, without an object, and the meaning is not that they spread such-and-such. It is said "nashara al-mayyit" (the dead one came back to life), and "anshara-hu Allah" when God gives him life. So the meaning would be the souls that were given life by the 'urf with which the mursalat were sent, or the bodies and spirits and lands that were given life by the sent winds. The winds are a cause for the resurrection of bodies and plants, and revelation is a cause for the resurrection and life of spirits. But there is a matter that must be noticed here: God, glory be to Him, made the oaths in this surah of two kinds, and separated one from the other. He made al-'asifat conjoined to al-mursalat with the fa' of sequence, so they became as if they were one type.

Then He made al-nashirat as if it were a new oath, and He introduced it with the waw. Then He conjoined al-fariqat and al-mulqiyat to it with the fa', which gives the impression that al-fariqat and al-mulqiyat are connected to al-nashirat, and that al-'asifat is connected to al-mursalat.

There is disagreement about al-fariqat (those that separate), but most hold that they are the angels. This is shown by the conjunction of "al-mulqiyat dhikran" (those that deliver the reminder) to them with the fa', and al-mulqiyat are the angels by agreement.

On this view, the oath is by the angels who spread their wings at descent, so they separate truth from falsehood, and they deliver the reminder to the messengers as an excuse or as a warning.

Whoever takes al-nashirat to be the winds takes al-fariqat as a description of them and says: they separate the clouds here and there.

But the conjunction of al-mulqiyat with the fa' to it rejects this.

Whoever says al-fariqat means the Qur'an, which separates truth from falsehood, his statement fits better with al-nashirat being the angels than it does if it is said they are the winds.

Whoever says they are groups of messengers: if he means messengers from among the angels, then it is clear. If he means messengers from among humans, the weakness of this view has already been explained.

It appears to me—and God knows best what He meant by His words—that the oath in this verse falls upon both types: the winds and the angels.

The point of connection is that the life of the earth, of plants, and of the bodies of animals is by the winds, for they are from the spirit of God, and God has made them a resurrection (nushur). And the life of the hearts and spirits is by the angels.

By these two types, the two kinds of life are attained. This is why, and God knows best, He separated one of the two types from the other with the waw, and made what is a follower of each type come after it with the fa'.

Consider how the oath in this surah falls upon the return (ma'ad) and the everlasting, enduring life, and the condition of the blessed and the wretched in it. He established this by the first life in His saying: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ (77:20). In it He mentioned the origin and the return, and He made the surah devoted to this. So it was fitting to swear by what achieves the two kinds of visible life, which are the winds and the angels.

So in the oath by these, there is the clearest proof and the most manifest sign of the truth of what He swore upon and what the surah contains. This is why the denier after that is in the utmost denial, obstinacy, and disbelief, and deserves woe upon woe, and his woe is doubled just as his disbelief and denial were doubled.

There is no better repetition than this in this place, nor one more significant in its effect. It is repeated ten times, and it is mentioned only after a proof or something indicated by a proof, following what necessitates belief and what necessitates believing in it. So reflect on this.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿as an excuse or as a warning﴾ (77:6)

(Section)

Some people say: among the completions of repentance is abandoning making excuses (i'tidhar), for making excuses is an argument against the offense, while abandoning excuses is an acknowledgment of it, and repentance is not valid except after acknowledgment. Regarding this, one of the poets said to his superior, when he had blamed him for something:

"You did not meet your reproach with an excuse, but I say what you say.
And I knock at the door of your pardon with humility, and good character judges between us."

When the superior heard his words, he stood up, rode to him immediately, and removed his blame.

So the completion of acknowledgment is abandoning excuses, by having in his heart and tongue: "O God, I have no innocence from sin so that I might make an excuse, and I have no strength so that I might prevail. Rather, I am a sinner seeking forgiveness. O God, I have no excuse; it is purely Your right and purely my offense. If You pardon, well and good; otherwise the right is Yours."

What appears to me from the words of the author of Manazil al-Sa'irin is that by making excuses he meant showing weakness and humility, the enemy's dominance, and the strength of the authority of the soul. He meant that what came from me was not out of contempt for Your right, nor out of ignorance of it, nor out of denying Your knowledge, nor out of making light of Your threat. Rather, it came from the overpowering of desire and the weakness of strength to resist the sickness of lust, and out of hope for Your forgiveness, reliance on Your pardon, good opinion of You, hope in Your generosity, and desire for the vastness of Your forbearance and mercy. The delusion deceived me about You, along with the commanding soul to evil, and Your concealing veil over me. My ignorance aided me, and there is no way to seek protection for me except through You, and no help for obedience to You except through Your guidance. And similar to this are words containing supplication, humbling oneself, need, acknowledgment of incapacity, and affirmation of servitude.

This is among the completions of repentance. Only the wise, who seek to win favor with their Lord, mighty and majestic, adopt it, and God loves that His servant seek to win His favor.

In a hadith: "Seek to win God's favor." And in the Sahih (the authentic collection of hadith): "No one loves excuse more than God." Even if its meaning is that of giving excuse (i'dhar), as He said at the end of the hadith: "For this reason He sent the messengers as bearers of good tidings and warners."

And He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Then those that deliver the reminder, as an excuse or as a warning﴾ (77:5–6). It is part of His perfect justice and kindness that He gave excuse to His servants, and that He does not punish their wrongdoers except after the full giving of excuse and the establishment of proof against them. So He also loves that His servant make excuse before Him and seek release from his sin before Him.

In a hadith: "Whoever makes excuse to God, God accepts his excuse."

This is the praiseworthy and beneficial excuse.

As for making excuses by destiny (al-qadar), it is a contesting with God and an argument by the servant against the Lord, and placing the blame for his sin upon the decrees. This is the act of God's adversaries, as one of their shaykhs said regarding His saying: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾ (3:14). He said: "Do you know what is meant by this verse?" They said: "What is meant by it?" He said: "The establishing of excuses for creation."

This ignorant man lied about God and His speech. What is meant by it is to discourage from this perishing, passing world, to encourage the enduring, lasting one, and to disparage those who prefer this adorned thing and follow it. It is like a child to whom are shown toys to play with, so he becomes excited by them and moves toward them, although the one who adorned them is not mentioned. So He did not say "We were adorned for people." God, Exalted is He, attributes the adorning of the world and of sins to the devils, as He said: ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear good to them﴾ (6:43), and He said: ﴿And thus their partners have made the killing of their children appear attractive to many of the polytheists﴾ (6:137).

In a hadith: "I was sent as a guide and a caller, and I have no share of guidance. Iblis was sent as a misleader and one who adorns, and he has no share of error." This does not contradict His saying: ﴿Thus We made attractive to every community its deeds﴾ (6:108).

For the attribution of adorning to Him is by decree and destiny, while its attribution to Satan is by causation. Moreover, His adorning is a punishment for them for their inclination toward what Satan had adorned for them. So among the punishment for an evil deed is another evil deed after it, and among the reward for a good deed is another good deed after it.

The point is that argument by destiny contradicts repentance, and it is not part of making excuse at all. In some reports: "When the servant sins and says: 'O Lord, this is Your decree, You have predestined it for me, You have judged it for me, You have written it for me,' God, mighty and majestic, says: 'You did it, You earned it, You willed it and strove for it, and I will punish you for it.' And when he says: 'O Lord, I wronged myself, I erred, I transgressed, I did it,' God, mighty and majestic, says: 'I had power over you, I decreed it, I wrote it, and I forgive you.' And when he does a good deed and says: 'O Lord, I did it, I gave charity, I prayed, I fed,' God, mighty and majestic, says: 'I helped you, I granted you success.' And when he says: 'O Lord, You helped me and granted me success, and You bestowed favor upon me,' God says: 'You did it, You willed it, You earned it.'"

So making excuse is of two kinds: an excuse that negates acknowledgment, which contradicts repentance; and an excuse that affirms acknowledgment, which is part of the completion of repentance.

(Section: Mention of a debate between two jurists on the purity and impurity of semen)

The one who claims purity said: Semen is the origin of the creation of a human being, so it is pure, like dust.

The other said: How far off is your comparison! Dust has been placed as a purifier and as an aid to purification in the case of licking (wulugh), and according to one opinion it removes the ruling of minor impurity (hadath), and according to another, the impurity itself. So what is used for purification is far from what is purified from. Moreover, transformations (istihalat) do their work. So how can the secondary things be compared to their origins? Is wine anything but the daughter of the grape? And semen is nothing but what is produced from foods in the stomach, which transforms them into impurity, then into blood, then into semen.

The purifier said: What you mentioned about dust is correct. But the fact that semen is something one purifies from does not indicate its impurity: intercourse without emission is also something one purifies from. If purification from it were because of its impurity, purification would be restricted to the organs of wudu', like urine and blood. As for dust being a purifier while semen is not, this is because purification with semen cannot be conceived. Likewise its aiding in the case of licking. How far off is your distinction! As for your claim that transformation does its work, yes, it does: it turns good into foul, as foods turn into urine, feces and blood; and foul into good, as menstrual blood turns into milk, and as milk emerges from between the digestive matter and the blood. So transformation is among our greatest proofs against you, because semen is blood that desire has shortened and transformed, and it has changed from that into another substance. If you gave transformation its due, you would judge it pure.

The one who claims impurity said: Madhi is the origin of semen, and the Law has shown its impurity, since it commanded washing the penis and whatever is touched by it. And if its origin is impure, how much more so its end? And it is known that the origin exists in reality actually.

The purifier said: This is a claim without evidence. From where do you know that madhi is the origin of semen, when they are two realities different in essence, attributes, accidents, smell and nature? Your claim that madhi is the origin of semen and that it is semen not fully cooked is a bare claim, devoid of transmitted, rational and sensory evidence, so it is not accepted. Even if we granted it to you, it would benefit you nothing at all, for origins have rulings that differ from the rulings of secondary things. Blood is the origin of milk, and their rulings differ. Indeed, this semen itself is the origin of the human being, who is pure in substance, while its origin, according to you, is impure in substance. This is one of the clearest things that corrupts your argument and makes your contradiction plain, and there is no way to avert it. For if semen were impure in substance, the human being would not be pure, because according to you impurity is not purified by transformation. So one of your two principles must be abandoned: either you say semen is pure, or you say impurity is purified by transformation; or you say semen is impure and impurity is not purified by transformation, and then you say the human being is pure, which is a contradiction. We have nothing but to reject it.

The one who claims impurity said: Undoubtedly semen is a surplus substance transformed from food, which exits through the passage of urine, so it is impure like it. This does not apply to saliva, mucus, tears and sweat, because they do not exit through the passage of urine.

The purifier said: Your judgment of impurity is either because of its transformation from food, or because of its exit through the passage of urine, or because of both together. The first is invalid, for the mere transformation of a surplus from food does not require a ruling of its impurity, like tears, mucus and saliva. If it is because it exits through the passage of urine, this only shows that it is contaminated by the impurity of its channel, not that it is impure in substance, which is one of the opinions about it, and it is corrupt. For the channel and the inner place of residence are not judged impure; impurity is judged only after exit and separation, and the separated substance is judged impure because of its own foulness and substance, not because of its channel or its place of residence. It has thus become clear that reliance on the combination of both is invalid. What makes this clear is that we see surplus substances transformed from food divided into pure ones, like saliva, sweat and mucus, and impure ones, like urine and feces. This shows that the aspect of transformation does not necessitate impurity. We also see that impurity revolves with foulness, existence and non-existence. Urine and feces are two foul, stinking, harmful substances, distinguished from the rest of human surplus by an excess of foulness, stench and filthiness; souls recoil from them and keep them as far away as possible. This is not the case with this noble surplus, which is the origin of the best of God's servants and their masters, and which is among the most noble substances of the human being and the finest parts separated from him, and with it is a spirit of life that distinguishes it from all other surpluses. To analogize it to excrement is the most corrupt analogy in the world and the furthest from correctness. God, the Exalted, is too wise to make the place of His revelation, His messages and the origin of His nearest ones impure. He is more generous than that. Moreover, God, the Exalted, informed about this water and repeated the report about it in the Qur'an, describing it again and again. He told that it is a gushing fluid that issues from between the loins and the ribs, and that He deposited it in a secure place. God would not repeat mention of a thing like excrement and urine, return to it, display it and inform that it is kept in a secure place, describing it with its best attributes such as gushing and others. He described it with humility only to manifest His absolute power, that He created from this weak water this strong, well-proportioned human being. So the "despised" here is the weak, not the impure and foul. Moreover, if semen were impure, and everything impure is foul, God would not have made it the origin of the creation of the good servants and the good things. That is why no good thing is produced from urine and feces. Whoever made the origins of the children of Adam impure and unclean has strayed far. When people revile a man, they say: his origin is foul, and he is foul in origin. If the origins of people were impure and everything impure is foul, this reproach would be like saying his origin is a drop or his origin is water, and the like. And if they mean by foulness of origin that the drop was placed in other than its proper state, that is foulness upon foulness. God did not place any impurity in the origins of the special servants in any way.

The impurity-claimers said: You have greatly reproached us with the impurity of the origin of the human being, you have prolonged the discussion, and you have gone too far. That reproach applies equally to both of us, for just as God makes His special servants containers and vessels for impurities like urine, feces, blood and madhi, without this reflecting on them as a defect or blame, so too His creating them from impure semen is the same. What is the difference?

The purifiers said: You have clung to what you have no grounds for, and taken comfort in a false imagination. They are not containers of impurity at all. Surplus becomes urine and feces only when it separates from its place, and then it is judged impure. As long as it is in its place, it is food and good drink, not foul. It becomes foul only after it is ejected and expelled. Likewise blood is impure only when it is poured out and flows; as long as it is in the body of the animal and its veins, it is not impure. The believer does not become impure, nor is he a container for filth and impurities.

They said: What cuts off the root of the claim of impurity is that the Prophet ﷺ knew that the community was greatly afflicted with it in their bodies, clothes, bedding and quilts, yet he never once commanded them to wash what touched them, neither from the body nor from a garment at all. It is impossible that it would be like urine, and he never gave them a single word commanding its washing; and delaying clarification beyond the time of need is impermissible for him.

They also said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ are the most knowledgeable of the community about the ruling in this matter. It is established from 'Aisha that she objected to a man to whom she had lent a yellow quilt, and who slept in it and had a wet dream, and he washed it; she objected to his washing it and said: "It would have sufficed him to rub it with his finger; I would often rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ with my finger." Ibn Abi Shaybah reported it: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us from al-A'mash from Ibrahim from Hammam, who said: A guest came to 'Aisha, and he mentioned it. He also said: Hushaym narrated to us from Mughirah from Ibrahim from al-Aswad from 'Aisha, who said: "I used to find it on the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ and I would scrape it off," meaning semen. This is also the view of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Hushaym narrated to us from Husayn from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from Sa'd that "he used to rub off the janabah from his garment." Jarir narrated to us from Mansur from Mujahid from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from Sa'd that "he used to rub off janabah from his garment." Waki' narrated to us from Sufyan from Habib from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas concerning semen: "Wipe it with an idhkhira (a sweet reed grass)." Hushaym narrated to us, informing us from Hajjaj and Ibn Abi Layla from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas concerning janabah that gets on a garment: "It is only like phlegm or spittle; remove it from you with a rag or an idhkhira."

They also said: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal reported in his Musnad from the hadith of 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to wipe semen from his garment with a sprig of idhkhir, then pray in it, and he would scrape it dry from his garment, then pray in it." This is explicit in its purity and admits of no interpretation whatsoever.

They also said: al-Daraqutni reported from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq: Shurayk narrated to us from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said:

"The Prophet ﷺ was asked about semen that gets on a garment? He said: 'It is only like spittle and mucus, and it is enough for you to wipe it with a rag or an idhkhira.'"

They said: This chain is sound. Ishaq al-Azraq's narration is recorded in the two Sahihs, and so is Shurayk's. Although it was faulted on account of Ishaq al-Azraq's sole transmission of it, Ishaq is trustworthy and is relied upon in the two Sahihs, and according to you, a trustworthy narrator's single addition is accepted.

The impurity-claimer said: It is authentically reported from 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she used to wash it from the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it is established from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he ordered its washing.

Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us from Simak from 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas who said:

"If a man has janabah in his garment and sees a trace of it, let him wash it; and if he does not see a trace of it, let him sprinkle it."

'Abd al-A'la narrated to us from Ma'mar from al-Zuhri from Talhah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Awf from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that he used to say concerning janabah in a garment: "If you see its trace, wash it; and if you know that it has touched it and it is hidden from you, wash the garment in that place; and if you know it has touched it, wash the whole garment." Waki' narrated to us from Hisham from his father from Zayd ibn al-Salt: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab washed what he saw and sprinkled what he did not see, and repeated it after it had dried firmly." Waki' narrated to us from al-Sari ibn Yahya from 'Abd al-Karim ibn Rashid from Anas concerning a man who had janabah in his garment and did not see its trace: "Let him wash the whole of it."

Jabir narrated to us from Hafs from Ash'ath from al-Hakam that Ibn Mas'ud "used to wash the trace of wet dreams from his garment."

Husayn ibn 'Ali narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Burqan from Khalid ibn Abi 'Izzah, who said: A man asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "I had a wet dream on a mat?" He said: "If it is wet, wash it; if it is dry, scrape it; and if it is hidden from you, sprinkle it."

They said: It is established that semen is named "adha" (harm), just as menstrual blood is named adha, and adha means impurity. Al-Tahawi said: Rabi' al-Hayri narrated to us from Ishaq ibn Bakr ibn Mudar, who said: My father narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah from Yazid ibn Abi Habib from Suwayd ibn Qays from Mu'awiyah ibn Hudayj from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan that he asked his sister Umm Habibah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ: "Did the Prophet ﷺ pray in the garment in which he lay with you?" She said: "Yes, if it did not have adha on it."

This is evidence in another respect, namely that he abstained from praying in it. And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq narrated from 'Aisha who said: "The Messenger of God used to pray in the quilts of his wives."

They said: As for what you mentioned of the reports about wiping it with an idhkhira and rubbing it, they concern sleeping garments, not prayer garments. They said: We have seen that garments soiled with feces, urine and blood may be slept in without harm, but praying in them is not permitted. So it is possible that semen is likewise.

They said: Those reports would be a proof against us only if we said that sleeping in an impure garment is not permissible. Since we permit that and agree with what you have transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ regarding it, while saying afterward that prayer is not valid in it, we have contradicted nothing that was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ on this matter.

They said: Since the reports have differed in this chapter, and there is no evidence in them regarding the ruling on semen, we consider the matter by way of reasoning. We found that the emission of semen is a hadath of the most severe kind, for it requires the greatest purification. So we wished to examine things whose emission is a hadath, what their ruling is in themselves. We found that feces and urine, whose emission is a hadath, are impure in themselves; likewise menstrual and istihadah blood, which are hadath and impure in themselves; and blood from the veins is likewise in our consideration. Since it has been established by what we mentioned that whatever's emission is a hadath is impure in itself, and since it has been established that the emission of semen is a hadath, it is also established that it is impure in itself. This is our reasoning on it.

The purifier said: Nothing you have mentioned is evidence of its impurity. As for 'Aisha washing it from the garment of the Messenger of God, there is no doubt that a garment is washed from dirt, filth and impurity, so the mere washing of a garment from it does not indicate its impurity. She sometimes washed it, sometimes wiped it, and sometimes rubbed it; her rubbing and wiping is evidence of its purity, and washing does not indicate impurity. If you gave the evidences their due, you would know that they agree and corroborate one another, not that they contradict and conflict. As for Ibn 'Abbas's command to wash it, it is established from him that he said: "It is only like mucus and spittle, so remove it from you even with an idhkhira." His command to wash it was for cleanliness and removal of what is repugnant. Even if we grant that for him it was for impurity and that reports from him differed, it would be a matter of disagreement among the Companions, and proof would decide between the disputants. Moreover, we do not know of any Companion or anyone else who said that it is absolutely impure; rather the most that is related from the Companions is washing it, in action and command, and this does not entail impurity. If you took the totality of reports from them, they would indicate the permissibility of both: washing it for cleanliness, and being content with wiping it when wet and rubbing it when dry, like mucus. As for your statement that semen's naming as adha is established, that is not established. The words of Umm Habibah, "if it did not have adha on it," do not indicate that by adha she meant semen, neither by direct correspondence, nor by inclusion, nor by implication. She only reported that he prayed in the garment in which she lay with him, as long as no adha touched it, and she added nothing.

So if someone said: the intended meaning of adha is menstrual blood, your interpretation would be more fitting than yours. Likewise, his abstaining from praying in his wives' quilts does not indicate the impurity of semen at all, for a woman's quilt may be touched by her menstrual blood without her knowing it. The abstention may also be out of purity and seeking to pray in what is cleaner and more pure. So where is the evidence for making it impure?

As for your interpreting the reports that indicate being content with wiping and rubbing it as applying to sleeping garments rather than garments of purity, this is something your schools would necessitate. If you gave the hadiths their due, and examined their contexts and occasions, you would be certain that they were quoted to argue for purity by the Companions, and to object to those who deemed semen impure. 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "I used to rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God and he would pray in it." And in the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, both raised and stopped: "It is only like mucus and spittle, so remove it from you even with an idhkhira." In sum, it is impossible for it to be impure while the Prophet ﷺ knew how greatly the community was afflicted with it in their garments and bodies, and never commanded them on any day to wash it, while they knew that being content with wiping and rubbing it sufficed.

As for your statement that the reports differed in this chapter and there was nothing in what was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ explaining the ruling on semen, so you considered the matter by reasoning, it is said: the reports, praise be to God, are in agreement in this chapter, not in conflict, and all conditions of conflict are absent from them entirely. It has already been stated that washing at times and wiping and rubbing at other times are permissible, and that this indicates no contradiction or conflict at all. The Messenger of God ﷺ would not leave his community to mere reasoning and opinions on the ruling of this important matter, while he taught them everything, even relieving oneself and its etiquette. The Sunnah has explained this question in a complete explanation, and praise be to God.

As for what you mentioned, reasoning about its impurity, it is blind reasoning, because you derived the ruling of its impurity from the obligation of ritual bathing because of it, and there is no connection between them, neither rationally, nor legally, nor sensorily. The Lawgiver ruled that the whole body must be washed when it is emitted, just as He ruled it when the glans enters the vagina, and there is no impurity there or outside. This wind (ريح) requires washing the organs of wudu', yet it is not impure; that is why one does not cleanse oneself of it with water, nor wash the waist-wrap or garment of it. Not everything that necessitates purification is impure, nor is every impure thing necessarily one that requires purification. It is established from the Companions that they prayed after their blood flowed on numerous occasions, and they were too knowledgeable about God's religion to pray while in a state of hadath. So it becomes clear that reasoning does not necessitate its impurity, the reports indicate its purity, and God created substances on the basis of purity, so nothing among them becomes impure except what the Law has made impure. Whatever the Law has not made impure is on the original state of purity. And God knows best.

(Section: Mention of a debate between two jurists on the purity and impurity of semen)

The one who claims purity said: Semen is the origin of the creation of a human being, so it is pure, like dust.

The other said: How far off is your comparison! Dust has been placed as a purifier and as an aid to purification in the case of licking (wulugh), and according to one opinion it removes the ruling of minor impurity (hadath), and according to another, the impurity itself. So what is used for purification is far from what is purified from. Moreover, transformations (istihalat) do their work. So how can the secondary things be compared to their origins? Is wine anything but the daughter of the grape? And semen is nothing but what is produced from foods in the stomach, which transforms them into impurity, then into blood, then into semen.

The purifier said: What you mentioned about dust is correct. But the fact that semen is something one purifies from does not indicate its impurity: intercourse without emission is also something one purifies from. If purification from it were because of its impurity, purification would be restricted to the organs of wudu', like urine and blood. As for dust being a purifier while semen is not, this is because purification with semen cannot be conceived. Likewise its aiding in the case of licking. How far off is your distinction! As for your claim that transformation does its work, yes, it does: it turns good into foul, as foods turn into urine, feces and blood; and foul into good, as menstrual blood turns into milk, and as milk emerges from between the digestive matter and the blood. So transformation is among our greatest proofs against you, because semen is blood that desire has shortened and transformed, and it has changed from that into another substance. If you gave transformation its due, you would judge it pure.

The one who claims impurity said: Madhi is the origin of semen, and the Law has shown its impurity, since it commanded washing the penis and whatever is touched by it. And if its origin is impure, how much more so its end? And it is known that the origin exists in reality actually.

The purifier said: This is a claim without evidence. From where do you know that madhi is the origin of semen, when they are two realities different in essence, attributes, accidents, smell and nature? Your claim that madhi is the origin of semen and that it is semen not fully cooked is a bare claim, devoid of transmitted, rational and sensory evidence, so it is not accepted. Even if we granted it to you, it would benefit you nothing at all, for origins have rulings that differ from the rulings of secondary things. Blood is the origin of milk, and their rulings differ. Indeed, this semen itself is the origin of the human being, who is pure in substance, while its origin, according to you, is impure in substance. This is one of the clearest things that corrupts your argument and makes your contradiction plain, and there is no way to avert it. For if semen were impure in substance, the human being would not be pure, because according to you impurity is not purified by transformation. So one of your two principles must be abandoned: either you say semen is pure, or you say impurity is purified by transformation; or you say semen is impure and impurity is not purified by transformation, and then you say the human being is pure, which is a contradiction. We have nothing but to reject it.

The one who claims impurity said: Undoubtedly semen is a surplus substance transformed from food, which exits through the passage of urine, so it is impure like it. This does not apply to saliva, mucus, tears and sweat, because they do not exit through the passage of urine.

The purifier said: Your judgment of impurity is either because of its transformation from food, or because of its exit through the passage of urine, or because of both together. The first is invalid, for the mere transformation of a surplus from food does not require a ruling of its impurity, like tears, mucus and saliva. If it is because it exits through the passage of urine, this only shows that it is contaminated by the impurity of its channel, not that it is impure in substance, which is one of the opinions about it, and it is corrupt. For the channel and the inner place of residence are not judged impure; impurity is judged only after exit and separation, and the separated substance is judged impure because of its own foulness and substance, not because of its channel or its place of residence. It has thus become clear that reliance on the combination of both is invalid. What makes this clear is that we see surplus substances transformed from food divided into pure ones, like saliva, sweat and mucus, and impure ones, like urine and feces. This shows that the aspect of transformation does not necessitate impurity. We also see that impurity revolves with foulness, existence and non-existence. Urine and feces are two foul, stinking, harmful substances, distinguished from the rest of human surplus by an excess of foulness, stench and filthiness; souls recoil from them and keep them as far away as possible. This is not the case with this noble surplus, which is the origin of the best of God's servants and their masters, and which is among the most noble substances of the human being and the finest parts separated from him, and with it is a spirit of life that distinguishes it from all other surpluses. To analogize it to excrement is the most corrupt analogy in the world and the furthest from correctness. God, the Exalted, is too wise to make the place of His revelation, His messages and the origin of His nearest ones impure. He is more generous than that. Moreover, God, the Exalted, informed about this water and repeated the report about it in the Qur'an, describing it again and again. He told that it is a gushing fluid that issues from between the loins and the ribs, and that He deposited it in a secure place. God would not repeat mention of a thing like excrement and urine, return to it, display it and inform that it is kept in a secure place, describing it with its best attributes such as gushing and others. He described it with humility only to manifest His absolute power, that He created from this weak water this strong, well-proportioned human being. So the "despised" here is the weak, not the impure and foul. Moreover, if semen were impure, and everything impure is foul, God would not have made it the origin of the creation of the good servants and the good things. That is why no good thing is produced from urine and feces. Whoever made the origins of the children of Adam impure and unclean has strayed far. When people revile a man, they say: his origin is foul, and he is foul in origin. If the origins of people were impure and everything impure is foul, this reproach would be like saying his origin is a drop or his origin is water, and the like. And if they mean by foulness of origin that the drop was placed in other than its proper state, that is foulness upon foulness. God did not place any impurity in the origins of the special servants in any way.

The impurity-claimers said: You have greatly reproached us with the impurity of the origin of the human being, you have prolonged the discussion, and you have gone too far. That reproach applies equally to both of us, for just as God makes His special servants containers and vessels for impurities like urine, feces, blood and madhi, without this reflecting on them as a defect or blame, so too His creating them from impure semen is the same. What is the difference?

The purifiers said: You have clung to what you have no grounds for, and taken comfort in a false imagination. They are not containers of impurity at all. Surplus becomes urine and feces only when it separates from its place, and then it is judged impure. As long as it is in its place, it is food and good drink, not foul. It becomes foul only after it is ejected and expelled. Likewise blood is impure only when it is poured out and flows; as long as it is in the body of the animal and its veins, it is not impure. The believer does not become impure, nor is he a container for filth and impurities.

They said: What cuts off the root of the claim of impurity is that the Prophet ﷺ knew that the community was greatly afflicted with it in their bodies, clothes, bedding and quilts, yet he never once commanded them to wash what touched them, neither from the body nor from a garment at all. It is impossible that it would be like urine, and he never gave them a single word commanding its washing; and delaying clarification beyond the time of need is impermissible for him.

They also said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ are the most knowledgeable of the community about the ruling in this matter. It is established from 'Aisha that she objected to a man to whom she had lent a yellow quilt, and who slept in it and had a wet dream, and he washed it; she objected to his washing it and said: "It would have sufficed him to rub it with his finger; I would often rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ with my finger." Ibn Abi Shaybah reported it: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us from al-A'mash from Ibrahim from Hammam, who said: A guest came to 'Aisha, and he mentioned it. He also said: Hushaym narrated to us from Mughirah from Ibrahim from al-Aswad from 'Aisha, who said: "I used to find it on the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ and I would scrape it off," meaning semen. This is also the view of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Hushaym narrated to us from Husayn from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from Sa'd that "he used to rub off the janabah from his garment." Jarir narrated to us from Mansur from Mujahid from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from Sa'd that "he used to rub off janabah from his garment." Waki' narrated to us from Sufyan from Habib from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas concerning semen: "Wipe it with an idhkhira (a sweet reed grass)." Hushaym narrated to us, informing us from Hajjaj and Ibn Abi Layla from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas concerning janabah that gets on a garment: "It is only like phlegm or spittle; remove it from you with a rag or an idhkhira."

They also said: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal reported in his Musnad from the hadith of 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to wipe semen from his garment with a sprig of idhkhir, then pray in it, and he would scrape it dry from his garment, then pray in it." This is explicit in its purity and admits of no interpretation whatsoever.

They also said: al-Daraqutni reported from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq: Shurayk narrated to us from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said:

"The Prophet ﷺ was asked about semen that gets on a garment? He said: 'It is only like spittle and mucus, and it is enough for you to wipe it with a rag or an idhkhira.'"

They said: This chain is sound. Ishaq al-Azraq's narration is recorded in the two Sahihs, and so is Shurayk's. Although it was faulted on account of Ishaq al-Azraq's sole transmission of it, Ishaq is trustworthy and is relied upon in the two Sahihs, and according to you, a trustworthy narrator's single addition is accepted.

The impurity-claimer said: It is authentically reported from 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she used to wash it from the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it is established from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he ordered its washing.

Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us from Simak from 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas who said:

"If a man has janabah in his garment and sees a trace of it, let him wash it; and if he does not see a trace of it, let him sprinkle it."

'Abd al-A'la narrated to us from Ma'mar from al-Zuhri from Talhah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Awf from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that he used to say concerning janabah in a garment: "If you see its trace, wash it; and if you know that it has touched it and it is hidden from you, wash the garment in that place; and if you know it has touched it, wash the whole garment." Waki' narrated to us from Hisham from his father from Zayd ibn al-Salt: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab washed what he saw and sprinkled what he did not see, and repeated it after it had dried firmly." Waki' narrated to us from al-Sari ibn Yahya from 'Abd al-Karim ibn Rashid from Anas concerning a man who had janabah in his garment and did not see its trace: "Let him wash the whole of it."

Jabir narrated to us from Hafs from Ash'ath from al-Hakam that Ibn Mas'ud "used to wash the trace of wet dreams from his garment."

Husayn ibn 'Ali narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Burqan from Khalid ibn Abi 'Izzah, who said: A man asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "I had a wet dream on a mat?" He said: "If it is wet, wash it; if it is dry, scrape it; and if it is hidden from you, sprinkle it."

They said: It is established that semen is named "adha" (harm), just as menstrual blood is named adha, and adha means impurity. Al-Tahawi said: Rabi' al-Hayri narrated to us from Ishaq ibn Bakr ibn Mudar, who said: My father narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah from Yazid ibn Abi Habib from Suwayd ibn Qays from Mu'awiyah ibn Hudayj from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan that he asked his sister Umm Habibah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ: "Did the Prophet ﷺ pray in the garment in which he lay with you?" She said: "Yes, if it did not have adha on it."

This is evidence in another respect, namely that he abstained from praying in it. And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq narrated from 'Aisha who said: "The Messenger of God used to pray in the quilts of his wives."

They said: As for what you mentioned of the reports about wiping it with an idhkhira and rubbing it, they concern sleeping garments, not prayer garments. They said: We have seen that garments soiled with feces, urine and blood may be slept in without harm, but praying in them is not permitted. So it is possible that semen is likewise.

They said: Those reports would be a proof against us only if we said that sleeping in an impure garment is not permissible. Since we permit that and agree with what you have transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ regarding it, while saying afterward that prayer is not valid in it, we have contradicted nothing that was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ on this matter.

They said: Since the reports have differed in this chapter, and there is no evidence in them regarding the ruling on semen, we consider the matter by way of reasoning. We found that the emission of semen is a hadath of the most severe kind, for it requires the greatest purification. So we wished to examine things whose emission is a hadath, what their ruling is in themselves. We found that feces and urine, whose emission is a hadath, are impure in themselves; likewise menstrual and istihadah blood, which are hadath and impure in themselves; and blood from the veins is likewise in our consideration. Since it has been established by what we mentioned that whatever's emission is a hadath is impure in itself, and since it has been established that the emission of semen is a hadath, it is also established that it is impure in itself. This is our reasoning on it.

The purifier said: Nothing you have mentioned is evidence of its impurity. As for 'Aisha washing it from the garment of the Messenger of God, there is no doubt that a garment is washed from dirt, filth and impurity, so the mere washing of a garment from it does not indicate its impurity. She sometimes washed it, sometimes wiped it, and sometimes rubbed it; her rubbing and wiping is evidence of its purity, and washing does not indicate impurity. If you gave the evidences their due, you would know that they agree and corroborate one another, not that they contradict and conflict. As for Ibn 'Abbas's command to wash it, it is established from him that he said: "It is only like mucus and spittle, so remove it from you even with an idhkhira." His command to wash it was for cleanliness and removal of what is repugnant. Even if we grant that for him it was for impurity and that reports from him differed, it would be a matter of disagreement among the Companions, and proof would decide between the disputants. Moreover, we do not know of any Companion or anyone else who said that it is absolutely impure; rather the most that is related from the Companions is washing it, in action and command, and this does not entail impurity. If you took the totality of reports from them, they would indicate the permissibility of both: washing it for cleanliness, and being content with wiping it when wet and rubbing it when dry, like mucus. As for your statement that semen's naming as adha is established, that is not established. The words of Umm Habibah, "if it did not have adha on it," do not indicate that by adha she meant semen, neither by direct correspondence, nor by inclusion, nor by implication. She only reported that he prayed in the garment in which she lay with him, as long as no adha touched it, and she added nothing.

So if someone said: the intended meaning of adha is menstrual blood, your interpretation would be more fitting than yours. Likewise, his abstaining from praying in his wives' quilts does not indicate the impurity of semen at all, for a woman's quilt may be touched by her menstrual blood without her knowing it. The abstention may also be out of purity and seeking to pray in what is cleaner and more pure. So where is the evidence for making it impure?

As for your interpreting the reports that indicate being content with wiping and rubbing it as applying to sleeping garments rather than garments of purity, this is something your schools would necessitate. If you gave the hadiths their due, and examined their contexts and occasions, you would be certain that they were quoted to argue for purity by the Companions, and to object to those who deemed semen impure. 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "I used to rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God and he would pray in it." And in the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, both raised and stopped: "It is only like mucus and spittle, so remove it from you even with an idhkhira." In sum, it is impossible for it to be impure while the Prophet ﷺ knew how greatly the community was afflicted with it in their garments and bodies, and never commanded them on any day to wash it, while they knew that being content with wiping and rubbing it sufficed.

As for your statement that the reports differed in this chapter and there was nothing in what was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ explaining the ruling on semen, so you considered the matter by reasoning, it is said: the reports, praise be to God, are in agreement in this chapter, not in conflict, and all conditions of conflict are absent from them entirely. It has already been stated that washing at times and wiping and rubbing at other times are permissible, and that this indicates no contradiction or conflict at all. The Messenger of God ﷺ would not leave his community to mere reasoning and opinions on the ruling of this important matter, while he taught them everything, even relieving oneself and its etiquette. The Sunnah has explained this question in a complete explanation, and praise be to God.

As for what you mentioned, reasoning about its impurity, it is blind reasoning, because you derived the ruling of its impurity from the obligation of ritual bathing because of it, and there is no connection between them, neither rationally, nor legally, nor sensorily. The Lawgiver ruled that the whole body must be washed when it is emitted, just as He ruled it when the glans enters the vagina, and there is no impurity there or outside. This wind (ريح) requires washing the organs of wudu', yet it is not impure; that is why one does not cleanse oneself of it with water, nor wash the waist-wrap or garment of it. Not everything that necessitates purification is impure, nor is every impure thing necessarily one that requires purification. It is established from the Companions that they prayed after their blood flowed on numerous occasions, and they were too knowledgeable about God's religion to pray while in a state of hadath. So it becomes clear that reasoning does not necessitate its impurity, the reports indicate its purity, and God created substances on the basis of purity, so nothing among them becomes impure except what the Law has made impure. Whatever the Law has not made impure is on the original state of purity. And God knows best.

(Section: Mention of a debate between two jurists on the purity and impurity of semen)

The one who claims purity said: Semen is the origin of the creation of a human being, so it is pure, like dust.

The other said: How far off is your comparison! Dust has been placed as a purifier and as an aid to purification in the case of licking (wulugh), and according to one opinion it removes the ruling of minor impurity (hadath), and according to another, the impurity itself. So what is used for purification is far from what is purified from. Moreover, transformations (istihalat) do their work. So how can the secondary things be compared to their origins? Is wine anything but the daughter of the grape? And semen is nothing but what is produced from foods in the stomach, which transforms them into impurity, then into blood, then into semen.

The purifier said: What you mentioned about dust is correct. But the fact that semen is something one purifies from does not indicate its impurity: intercourse without emission is also something one purifies from. If purification from it were because of its impurity, purification would be restricted to the organs of wudu', like urine and blood. As for dust being a purifier while semen is not, this is because purification with semen cannot be conceived. Likewise its aiding in the case of licking. How far off is your distinction! As for your claim that transformation does its work, yes, it does: it turns good into foul, as foods turn into urine, feces and blood; and foul into good, as menstrual blood turns into milk, and as milk emerges from between the digestive matter and the blood. So transformation is among our greatest proofs against you, because semen is blood that desire has shortened and transformed, and it has changed from that into another substance. If you gave transformation its due, you would judge it pure.

The one who claims impurity said: Madhi is the origin of semen, and the Law has shown its impurity, since it commanded washing the penis and whatever is touched by it. And if its origin is impure, how much more so its end? And it is known that the origin exists in reality actually.

The purifier said: This is a claim without evidence. From where do you know that madhi is the origin of semen, when they are two realities different in essence, attributes, accidents, smell and nature? Your claim that madhi is the origin of semen and that it is semen not fully cooked is a bare claim, devoid of transmitted, rational and sensory evidence, so it is not accepted. Even if we granted it to you, it would benefit you nothing at all, for origins have rulings that differ from the rulings of secondary things. Blood is the origin of milk, and their rulings differ. Indeed, this semen itself is the origin of the human being, who is pure in substance, while its origin, according to you, is impure in substance. This is one of the clearest things that corrupts your argument and makes your contradiction plain, and there is no way to avert it. For if semen were impure in substance, the human being would not be pure, because according to you impurity is not purified by transformation. So one of your two principles must be abandoned: either you say semen is pure, or you say impurity is purified by transformation; or you say semen is impure and impurity is not purified by transformation, and then you say the human being is pure, which is a contradiction. We have nothing but to reject it.

The one who claims impurity said: Undoubtedly semen is a surplus substance transformed from food, which exits through the passage of urine, so it is impure like it. This does not apply to saliva, mucus, tears and sweat, because they do not exit through the passage of urine.

The purifier said: Your judgment of impurity is either because of its transformation from food, or because of its exit through the passage of urine, or because of both together. The first is invalid, for the mere transformation of a surplus from food does not require a ruling of its impurity, like tears, mucus and saliva. If it is because it exits through the passage of urine, this only shows that it is contaminated by the impurity of its channel, not that it is impure in substance, which is one of the opinions about it, and it is corrupt. For the channel and the inner place of residence are not judged impure; impurity is judged only after exit and separation, and the separated substance is judged impure because of its own foulness and substance, not because of its channel or its place of residence. It has thus become clear that reliance on the combination of both is invalid. What makes this clear is that we see surplus substances transformed from food divided into pure ones, like saliva, sweat and mucus, and impure ones, like urine and feces. This shows that the aspect of transformation does not necessitate impurity. We also see that impurity revolves with foulness, existence and non-existence. Urine and feces are two foul, stinking, harmful substances, distinguished from the rest of human surplus by an excess of foulness, stench and filthiness; souls recoil from them and keep them as far away as possible. This is not the case with this noble surplus, which is the origin of the best of God's servants and their masters, and which is among the most noble substances of the human being and the finest parts separated from him, and with it is a spirit of life that distinguishes it from all other surpluses. To analogize it to excrement is the most corrupt analogy in the world and the furthest from correctness. God, the Exalted, is too wise to make the place of His revelation, His messages and the origin of His nearest ones impure. He is more generous than that. Moreover, God, the Exalted, informed about this water and repeated the report about it in the Qur'an, describing it again and again. He told that it is a gushing fluid that issues from between the loins and the ribs, and that He deposited it in a secure place. God would not repeat mention of a thing like excrement and urine, return to it, display it and inform that it is kept in a secure place, describing it with its best attributes such as gushing and others. He described it with humility only to manifest His absolute power, that He created from this weak water this strong, well-proportioned human being. So the "despised" here is the weak, not the impure and foul. Moreover, if semen were impure, and everything impure is foul, God would not have made it the origin of the creation of the good servants and the good things. That is why no good thing is produced from urine and feces. Whoever made the origins of the children of Adam impure and unclean has strayed far. When people revile a man, they say: his origin is foul, and he is foul in origin. If the origins of people were impure and everything impure is foul, this reproach would be like saying his origin is a drop or his origin is water, and the like. And if they mean by foulness of origin that the drop was placed in other than its proper state, that is foulness upon foulness. God did not place any impurity in the origins of the special servants in any way.

The impurity-claimers said: You have greatly reproached us with the impurity of the origin of the human being, you have prolonged the discussion, and you have gone too far. That reproach applies equally to both of us, for just as God makes His special servants containers and vessels for impurities like urine, feces, blood and madhi, without this reflecting on them as a defect or blame, so too His creating them from impure semen is the same. What is the difference?

The purifiers said: You have clung to what you have no grounds for, and taken comfort in a false imagination. They are not containers of impurity at all. Surplus becomes urine and feces only when it separates from its place, and then it is judged impure. As long as it is in its place, it is food and good drink, not foul. It becomes foul only after it is ejected and expelled. Likewise blood is impure only when it is poured out and flows; as long as it is in the body of the animal and its veins, it is not impure. The believer does not become impure, nor is he a container for filth and impurities.

They said: What cuts off the root of the claim of impurity is that the Prophet ﷺ knew that the community was greatly afflicted with it in their bodies, clothes, bedding and quilts, yet he never once commanded them to wash what touched them, neither from the body nor from a garment at all. It is impossible that it would be like urine, and he never gave them a single word commanding its washing; and delaying clarification beyond the time of need is impermissible for him.

They also said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ are the most knowledgeable of the community about the ruling in this matter. It is established from 'Aisha that she objected to a man to whom she had lent a yellow quilt, and who slept in it and had a wet dream, and he washed it; she objected to his washing it and said: "It would have sufficed him to rub it with his finger; I would often rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ with my finger." Ibn Abi Shaybah reported it: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us from al-A'mash from Ibrahim from Hammam, who said: A guest came to 'Aisha, and he mentioned it. He also said: Hushaym narrated to us from Mughirah from Ibrahim from al-Aswad from 'Aisha, who said: "I used to find it on the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ and I would scrape it off," meaning semen. This is also the view of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Hushaym narrated to us from Husayn from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from Sa'd that "he used to rub off the janabah from his garment." Jarir narrated to us from Mansur from Mujahid from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from Sa'd that "he used to rub off janabah from his garment." Waki' narrated to us from Sufyan from Habib from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas concerning semen: "Wipe it with an idhkhira (a sweet reed grass)." Hushaym narrated to us, informing us from Hajjaj and Ibn Abi Layla from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas concerning janabah that gets on a garment: "It is only like phlegm or spittle; remove it from you with a rag or an idhkhira."

They also said: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal reported in his Musnad from the hadith of 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to wipe semen from his garment with a sprig of idhkhir, then pray in it, and he would scrape it dry from his garment, then pray in it." This is explicit in its purity and admits of no interpretation whatsoever.

They also said: al-Daraqutni reported from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq: Shurayk narrated to us from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said:

They said: This chain is sound. Ishaq al-Azraq's narration is recorded in the two Sahihs, and so is Shurayk's. Although it was faulted on account of Ishaq al-Azraq's sole transmission of it, Ishaq is trustworthy and is relied upon in the two Sahihs, and according to you, a trustworthy narrator's single addition is accepted.

The impurity-claimer said: It is authentically reported from 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she used to wash it from the garment of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it is established from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he ordered its washing.

Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us from Simak from 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas who said:

"If a man has janabah in his garment and sees a trace of it, let him wash it; and if he does not see a trace of it, let him sprinkle it."

They said: As for what you mentioned of the reports about wiping it with an idhkhira and rubbing it, they concern sleeping garments, not prayer garments. They said: We have seen that garments soiled with feces, urine and blood may be slept in without harm, but praying in them is not permitted. So it is possible that semen is likewise.

They said: Those reports would be a proof against us only if we said that sleeping in an impure garment is not permissible. Since we permit that and agree with what you have transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ regarding it, while saying afterward that prayer is not valid in it, we have contradicted nothing that was transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ on this matter.

They said: Since the reports have differed in this chapter, and there is no evidence in them regarding the ruling on semen, we consider the matter by way of reasoning. We found that the emission of semen is a hadath of the most severe kind, for it requires the greatest purification. So we wished to examine things whose emission is a hadath, what their ruling is in themselves. We found that feces and urine, whose emission is a hadath, are impure in themselves; likewise menstrual and istihadah blood, which are hadath and impure in themselves; and blood from the veins is likewise in our consideration. Since it has been established by what we mentioned that whatever's emission is a hadath is impure in itself, and since it has been established that the emission of semen is a hadath, it is also established that it is impure in itself. This is our reasoning on it.

The purifier said: Nothing you have mentioned is evidence of its impurity. As for 'Aisha washing it from the garment of the Messenger of God, there is no doubt that a garment is washed from dirt, filth and impurity, so the mere washing of a garment from it does not indicate its impurity. She sometimes washed it, sometimes wiped it, and sometimes rubbed it; her rubbing and wiping is evidence of its purity, and washing does not indicate impurity. If you gave the evidences their due, you would know that they agree and corroborate one another, not that they contradict and conflict. As for Ibn 'Abbas's command to wash it, it is established from him that he said: "It is only like mucus and spittle, so remove it from you even with an idhkhira." His command to wash it was for cleanliness and removal of what is repugnant. Even if we grant that for him it was for impurity and that reports from him differed, it would be a matter of disagreement among the Companions, and proof would decide between the disputants. Moreover, we do not know of any Companion or anyone else who said that it is absolutely impure; rather the most that is related from the Companions is washing it, in action and command, and this does not entail impurity. If you took the totality of reports from them, they would indicate the permissibility of both: washing it for cleanliness, and being content with wiping it when wet and rubbing it when dry, like mucus. The words of Umm Habibah, "if it did not have adha on it," do not indicate that by adha she meant semen, neither by direct correspondence, nor by inclusion, nor by implication. She only reported that he prayed in the garment in which she lay with him, as long as no adha touched it, and she added nothing.

So if someone said: the intended meaning of adha is menstrual blood, your interpretation would be more fitting than yours. Likewise, his abstaining from praying in his wives' quilts does not indicate the impurity of semen at all, for a woman's quilt may be touched by her menstrual blood without her knowing it. The abstention may also be out of purity and seeking to pray in what is cleaner and more pure. So where is the evidence for making it impure?

If you gave the hadiths their due, and examined their contexts and occasions, you would be certain that they were quoted to argue for purity by the Companions, and to object to those who deemed semen impure. 'Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "I used to rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God and he would pray in it." And in the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, both raised and stopped: "It is only like mucus and spittle, so remove it from you even with an idhkhira."
