It has already been stated that washing at times and wiping and rubbing at other times are permissible, and that this indicates no contradiction or conflict at all. The Messenger of God ﷺ would not leave his community to mere reasoning and opinions on the ruling of this important matter, while he taught them everything, even relieving oneself and its etiquette. The Sunnah has explained this question in a complete explanation, and praise be to God.

As for what you mentioned, reasoning about its impurity, it is blind reasoning, because you derived the ruling of its impurity from the obligation of ritual bathing because of it, and there is no connection between them, neither rationally, nor legally, nor sensorily. The Lawgiver ruled that the whole body must be washed when it is emitted, just as He ruled it when the glans enters the vagina, and there is no impurity there or outside. This wind (ريح) requires washing the organs of wudu', yet it is not impure; that is why one does not cleanse oneself of it with water, nor wash the waist-wrap or garment of it. Not everything that necessitates purification is impure, nor is every impure thing necessarily one that requires purification. It is established from the Companions that they prayed after their blood flowed on numerous occasions, and they were too knowledgeable about God's religion to pray while in a state of hadath. So it becomes clear that reasoning does not necessitate its impurity, the reports indicate its purity, and God created substances on the basis of purity, so nothing among them becomes impure except what the Law has made impure. Whatever the Law has not made impure is on the original state of purity. And God knows best.

(Section: On the mention of the food and drink of the people of Paradise and their disposal)

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in shade and springs, and fruits of whatever they desire. "Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do."﴾

And He the Exalted says: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account." So he will be in a pleasant life, in a lofty garden, its clusters of fruit near at hand. "Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forward in the days past."﴾

And He the Exalted says: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do. For you therein is abundant fruit from which you will eat.﴾ And He the Exalted says: ﴿The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: beneath it rivers flow. Its food is eternal, and its shade.﴾

And He the Exalted says: ﴿And We provided them with fruit and meat of whatever they desire. They will pass around therein a cup, free of idle talk and sinful conduct.﴾

And He the Exalted says: ﴿They will be given to drink of sealed pure wine, whose seal is musk; and for that let the competitors compete.﴾

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"The people of Paradise eat and drink, but they do not blow their noses, nor defecate, nor urinate. Their food is belching like the scent of musk. They are inspired to glorify and magnify Allah as you are inspired to breathe."

It is also narrated by him from the narration of Talhah ibn Nafi from Jabir, in which it says: They said, "What about the food?" He said: "Belching and perspiration like the perspiration of musk. They are inspired to glorify and praise Allah."

In the Musnad and the Sunan of al-Nasa'i, with a sound chain meeting the conditions of the Sahih, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Thumamah ibn Uqbah, from Yazid ibn Arqam, who said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you claim that the people of Paradise eat and drink?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, indeed one of them will be given the strength of a hundred men in eating, drinking, sexual intercourse and desire."

He said: "But the one who eats and drinks has needs, and there is no harm in Paradise?" He said:

"The need of one of them is perspiration that flows from their skins like the perspiration of musk, so his belly becomes slim."

It is also narrated by al-Hakim in his Sahih, with the wording: A Jew came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, do you not claim that the people of Paradise eat therein and drink?" He said to his companions, "If he acknowledges this to me, I will refute him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, indeed one of them will be given the strength of a hundred men in eating, drinking, desire and intercourse." The Jew said to him: "But the one who eats and drinks has needs." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Their need is sweat that flows from their skins like musk, and then the belly becomes slim."

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah said: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "You will look at the bird in Paradise and desire it, and it will fall before you roasted."

The hadith of Anas concerning the story of Abdullah ibn Salam about the first food the people of Paradise eat and their drink has already been mentioned, following it, and the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "On the Day of Resurrection the earth will be a single loaf which the Almighty will turn over in His hand as a provision for the people of Paradise."

Al-Hakim said: al-Asamm informed us, Ibrahim ibn Munqidh narrated to us, Idris ibn Yahya narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah ibn Mawhab, from Ismah ibn Malik al-Khatmi, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there are birds like the Bukhti camels." Abu Bakr said: "They are indeed luxurious, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "More luxurious than them is the one who eats them, and you, Abu Bakr, are among those who eat them."

Al-Hakim said: al-Asamm informed us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata informed us, Sa'id informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying the Exalted: ﴿And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do not see the birds of Paradise as luxurious as its people are luxurious." He said: "The one who eats them is more luxurious than them, and they are like the Bukhti camels, and I hope with Allah that you will eat from them, O Abu Bakr."

And with this chain, from Qatadah, from Ayyub, a man from Basra, from Abdullah ibn Amr, concerning His saying the Exalted: ﴿They will be given rounds of gold and cups﴾, he said: Rounds of seventy plates of gold will be passed around to them, each plate containing a flavor not found in the others.

Allah, glorified is He, has informed that in Paradise there are shades, and shades must cast shadow over what is opposite them. He said: ﴿They and their spouses are in shade, reclining on couches﴾.

And He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in shade and springs﴾, and He said: ﴿And We will admit them to a shade, extensive﴾.

Foods, sweets, and incense require causes through which they are accomplished, and Allah, glorified is He, is the Creator of the cause and the caused, and He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything, there is no god but Him. Likewise, He, glorified is He, made for them causes that transform the food into belching and the perspiration that flows from their skins: this is the cause of its expulsion, and that is the cause of its maturation. Likewise, He placed in their bodies heat that cooks that food, refines it, and prepares it to come out as perspiration and belching. Likewise, the fruits and produce there are given heat that ripens them.

And He, glorified is He, makes the leaves of trees their shade. The Lord of this world and the Hereafter is one; He is the Creator of the causes and the wisdom, and what He creates in this world and the Hereafter is the same, and causes are a manifestation of His acts and wisdom, but they differ. For this reason the servant is astonished when His acts occur through causes other than the familiar, customary causes, and this may lead him to denial and disbelief, and that is pure ignorance and injustice. Otherwise, His power, glorified and exalted is He, is not limited to other causes and effects which He brings into being, just as His power is not limited in this observable world to its causes and effects, and this is no less easy for Him than that.

Perhaps the first creation which the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, brought into being in visible witness is more wondrous than the second creation which we were promised, if the intelligent person reflects upon it. Perhaps bringing these fruits and produce out of this coarse soil, water, wood and suitable air is more wondrous to reason than bringing them out of the soil, water and air of Paradise.

Perhaps bringing out these drinks, which are nourishment, medicine, drink and pleasure, from between dung and blood and from the vomit of flies, is more wondrous than causing them to flow as rivers in Paradise through other causes. Perhaps bringing out the jewels of gold and silver from the veins of stones in the mountains and elsewhere is more wondrous than producing them there through other causes. Perhaps bringing out silk from the saliva of the silkworm and its building for itself domes, white, red and yellow, most soundly built, is more wondrous than bringing it out of the sheaths that split from trees there, in which it was deposited and from which it was created. Perhaps the flow of the seas of water between heaven and earth upon the backs of clouds is more wondrous than their flowing in Paradise without a channel.

In sum, reflect upon the signs of Allah which He called His servants to contemplate and made signs indicating the perfection of His power, knowledge, will, wisdom and dominion, and His unity in lordship and divinity. Then weigh them against what He informed of concerning the Hereafter, Paradise and Hell, and you will find these the strongest proof of those, bearing witness to them, and you will find both from one niche, one Lord, one Creator and one Owner. So far away are the people who do not believe.

And He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in shade and springs﴾, and He said: ﴿And We will admit them to a shade, extensive﴾.

Foods, sweets, and incense require causes through which they are accomplished, and Allah, glorified is He, is the Creator of the cause and the caused, and He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything, there is no god but Him. Likewise, He, glorified is He, made for them causes that transform the food into belching and the perspiration that flows from their skins: this is the cause of its expulsion, and that is the cause of its maturation. Likewise, He placed in their bodies heat that cooks that food, refines it, and prepares it to come out as perspiration and belching. Likewise, the fruits and produce there are given heat that ripens them.

And He, glorified is He, makes the leaves of trees their shade. The Lord of this world and the Hereafter is one; He is the Creator of the causes and the wisdom, and what He creates in this world and the Hereafter is the same, and causes are a manifestation of His acts and wisdom, but they differ. So far away are the people who do not believe.

(Section: On the mention of the food and drink of the people of Paradise and their disposal)

And He the Exalted says: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account." Admonition.

Glory be to God! How many a widow's eye has wept, and how many an orphan's heart has burned, and how many a poor man's tear has flowed, while the wrongdoer lives in luxury. ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed, you are criminals.﴾
